14. Mr Monjur Kader, learned Deputy Attorney-General submits that legality of a similar case has been decided by the High Court Division as well us by the Hon'ble Appellate Division in the case of "Tarique Rahman vs Bangladesh", reported in 63 DLR (AD) 18. He submits that in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 1 of 2013 in the case of Giasuddin-al-Mamun vs State. In such a matter learned Senior Judge issued Rule while learned Second Judge and Third Judge rejected the application summarily. He submits that there is no substance and merit in the instant application and urge that Rule may not be issued in this matter. 

 15. It is admitted by the petitioner in paragraph No.6 of the revisional application that in a similar case where alleged offence was committed before the enactment of Money Laundering Prevention Act, 2009, Hon'ble Appellate Division held that the offence has been committed as alleged against the accused-petitioner should be tried under the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2002 under sections 2 (ট) (অ) (ই) and section 13 of the Money Laundering Protirodh Ain, 2002 as per judgment reported in 63 DLR (AD) 18. 

 16. I have gone through the decision of the referred case reported in 63 DLR (AD) 18 where- in co-accused Tarique Rahman preferred Writ Petition No. 6286 of 2010 before the High Court Division challenging the constitutional validity of the Money Laundering Protirodh Ain, 2009 and the legality of the initiation and continuation of the Anti-Corruption Commission GR Case No. 83 of 2009 arising out of Cantonment Police Station Case No.8 dated 26-10-2009 under section 2 and 4(2) of the Money Laundering Protirodh Ain, 2009. 

 (c) Offences Punishable under sections 161-169, 217, 218, 408, 409 and 477A of the Penal Code (XLV of 1860); 

 (d) Abetment described in section 109 including other abetments, conspiracies described in 120B, and attempts described in section 511 of the Penal Code, 1860 (XLV of 1860) related to or connected with the offences mentioned in clause (a) to (c) above." 

 (গ) The Penal Code, 1860 (Act XLV of 1860) এর sections 161-169,217,218,408,409 and 477 A এর অধীন শাস্তিযোগ্য অপরাধ সমূহ: 

 (ঘ) অনুচ্ছেদ (ক) হইতে (গ) তে বর্ণিত অপরাধ সমূহের সহিত সংশ্লিষ্ট বা সম্পৃক্ত The Penal Code, 1860 (Act XLV of 1860) এর section 109 এ বর্ণিত সহায়তা সহ অন্যান্য সহায়তা, এ বর্ণিত ষড়যন্ত্র এবং section 120B এ বর্ণিত ষড়যন্ত্র এবং section 511 এ বর্ণিত প্রচেষ্টার অপরাধ সমূহ।” 

 22. In the revisional application virtually the legality of the proceeding of the case has been challenged before us. Hon'ble Appellate Division in a similar case of "Tarique Rahman vs Bangladesh" reported in 63 DLR (AD) 18 decided that legislature has consciously included the Money Laundering Protirodh Ain, 2002 in the schedule to the Anti-Corruption Commission Act, 2004 as well as in the schedule to the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 and that any enquiry, investigation, lodging of the complaint, conducting of the prosecution before the Special Judge and holding of trial of the case exclusively by the Special Judge have been made required under the provisions of the Anti-Corruption Commission Act, 2004 and the same provision is equally applicable in the case of the offences under the Money Laundering Protirodh Ain. Furthermore, I have already discussed that their Lordships found the disclosure of the prima-facie case in the FIR, Investigation Report and other materials on record under sections 2(ট) (আ)(ই) and section 13 of the Money Laundering Protirodh Ain against the accused-persons of the said case and the prosecution can proceed, with the case in accordance with law under the Money Laundering Ain, 2002 since the alleged offence were committed during the operation of the Ain, 2002. 

 45. Mr Mahbub Uddin referring to the case of Tarique Rahman vs Government of Bangladesh, reported in 63 DLR (AD) 18 further submits that in the said case the Appellate Division having found prima-facie case under section 2 (ট)(আ)(অ) and section 13 of the Money Laundering Ain, 2002 against the accused of the said case held that prosecution may proceed with the case against the accused persons in accordance with law, if so advised; but in the instant case from the plain reading of the FIR and the charge-sheet it does not appear that any prima-facie case has been dis- closed under the Money Laundering Ain, 2002 or Ain, 2009 and, as such, taking cognizance into the case is absolutely illegal. He also submits that in the FIR it has been mentioned that in a Criminal Case held in District Court of Columbia, USA Siemens was found guilty as they admitted to have bribed various persons of Bangladesh in order to get a contract of BTCL but the present accused petitioner was not a party to the said case; even no finding has been given against the present accused petitioner. In this connection he has drawn my attention to paragraph 17 of the application, where the relevant portion of the judgment passed by the District Court of Columbia, USA has been quoted. 

 48. Mr Khurshid Alam Khan also appears on behalf of the opposite party No.2 Anti-Corruption Commission to resist the application. Mr Khan submits that the issues raised by the accused petitioner have already been settled in the cases of Tarique Rahman vs The State, reported in 63 DLR (AD) Page 18 and page 162 and Giasuddin-al-Mamun vs State, reported in 65 DLR 41. 

 59. Mr Mahbub Uddin, the learned Advocate for the accused petitioner has tried to impress me that the facts of the present case is quite distinguishable from the of case of Tarique Rahman vs Bangladesh, reported in 63 DLR (AD) 18.
